label: Figure 2.1
caption: Figure 2.1 The building control process
description: It is a vertical flowchart titled 'Figure 2.1 The building control process'. At the top, 'Start' leads to a decision box, 'Do Building Regulations apply to the work?', whose 'No' arrow points right to 'No notification required' and whose 'Yes' arrow points down to 'Has the work commenced?'. That box's 'No' arrow runs right to a statement that the work may be checked by the local authority or an approved inspector or carried out by a competent person; its 'Yes' arrow runs down to 'Apply to the local authority'. From that box a 'Yes' arrow runs down to a statement that the work may be checked by the local authority or an approved inspector and that work covered by a competent person scheme or a third-party scheme for certification can take place at the same time, and a 'No' arrow runs right to a decision on whether all the building work is covered by a competent person scheme or a third-party scheme for certification, whose 'Yes' arrow runs down to a statement that no notice need be submitted to the local authority because the competent person or the scheme operator will notify the local authority of the work and provide them and the building occupier with a certificate of completion within 30 days of completion of the work. Below these, two parallel columns of arrow-connected rectangular boxes appear, headed 'Local authority route' (magenta boxes) and 'Approved inspector route' (blue boxes). The left column begins with a box on local authority building control under the Building Regulations 2010, then a box on whether the work involves erecting or working on a building where the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 applies or will apply, erecting a building that fronts a private street, or erecting a building over a sewer, then boxes on the applicant depositing a full plans application or a building notice application, on the local authority providing a substantive assessment and consulting the fire authority and, where appropriate, the sewerage undertaker, on work starting after at least two clear working days' notice and being deemed at risk if the plans or details have not been assessed and approved, and on the local authority providing an inspection framework and issuing a completion certificate. The right column begins with a box on approved inspectors under the Building (Approved Inspectors etc.) Regulations 2010, then a box on an initial notice being given to the local authority in conjunction with the approved inspector, a decision on whether that initial notice is accepted (with a box to the right on providing additional information, amending the notice or submitting an application to the local authority if not), and then boxes on requesting plan assessment and a plans certificate, agreeing a site inspection plan with the approved inspector, the approved inspector consulting the fire authority and, where appropriate, the sewerage undertaker before the plans certificate or final certificate can be issued, and issuing a final certificate to both the applicant and the local authority within eight weeks of completion.
